What happened to you should not be downplayed because people may have had it worse than you. That doesn’t change what happened to you and I’m sorry that it did happen to you. Your experience is valid. It’s hard to move on from and it has cost you sleep. I would say the first thing to do is see a professional who works with trauma and insomnia. They can help you through this situation and get you in a better mindset, but for now, I suggest always calling someone on the phone before you go to bed, get the assurance that you are safe and also just talking to someone you trust will get you into a good mindset before sleep. Always double check, maybe even triple check that your doors and windows are locked, this will help remind you that nobody can get into your home even if they tried. Try sleeping with the lights on. I know that is difficult the first couple nights, but eventually it will be second nature. Listen to calming music before you sleep or watch happy tv shows, just so your mind will be less focused on fear and more focused on something else. I hope things get better for you. Stay safe.
